turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because lately, since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out. And then in the newsletter photos, I keep thinking my face looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t see it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation with perceived wrinkling/unevenness of their hands and facial crookedness that others reportedly do not see.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking these features throughout the day, such as looking at your hands or checking your reflection?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Before I teach a class or do a workshop at the senior center, I’ll go to the bathroom mirror a few times. I put lotion on my hands and turn my face different ways to check it. Sometimes I ask a coworker if I look all right. It can make me a little late getting started, but I still make it there.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeatedly checking the mirror, examining her face from different angles, applying lotion to her hands, and seeking reassurance about her appearance before classes or workshops.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you believe it is possible that your hands and face look normal and you are just viewing them more critically, or are you completely convinced of the flaw?
turns.patient_response: I’m not completely convinced, no. I mean, when I’m looking at them, it really does seem obvious to me, but I suppose it’s possible I’m being harder on myself than other people are.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports that perceived flaws in their hands and face seem obvious when viewed, while acknowledging they may be judging themselves more critically than others.
